title: Start with one useful result
subtitle: An original example about making a small tool understandable and usable.
thesis: The speaker argues that a small personal tool should first complete one useful path, show its evidence, and make its limits clear before expanding.

events.title: Choose the outcome
events.text: Define what a person can finish, not just what the tool contains.

events.title: Show the evidence
events.text: Connect a working result to its input and tested scope.

events.title: Improve from use
events.text: Let observed friction guide the next feature.

insights.title: Make one complete path work
insights.claim: The speaker puts a useful end result ahead of a long feature list. For a reading tool, the first successful path connects an important idea to the passage that supports it.
insights.example: A reader with limited time needs the argument, its evidence, and the conditions that might change the conclusion. Headings alone leave too much work to the reader.
insights.limit: Important qualifications should remain visible; hiding all of them can overstate the source.

details.title: A concrete reading task
details.text: The source describes someone who already has a transcript but needs the argument and its support without reading every line first.

insights.title: An example should show how it was made
insights.claim: The source asks for an input, a command, and the resulting file so someone else can follow the same path.
insights.example: A supplied-text example can exercise the page renderer while leaving podcast acquisition and difficult-audio recognition untested.
insights.limit: A successful reader demo is not evidence that every stage of a media pipeline works.

insights.title: Use real friction to choose the next change
insights.claim: The speaker prefers to observe repeated problems before adding features. A reader struggling to locate a passage needs better navigation; a confusing claim needs a clearer explanation.
insights.example: An account system would not resolve either of those problems. The suggested next check is to watch a new person use the tool without a live explanation.
insights.limit: The speaker limits this advice to a small personal tool, not every regulated or collaborative product.

details.title: After the first release
details.text: Record where a reader stops and state the limitation honestly before choosing the next improvement.

quotes.text: A clear boundary is more useful than an impressive promise.

notes: This is an original authored fixture, not a real podcast or an audio transcription. Its SRT timestamps are illustrative.
This sample verifies the supplied-text reader workflow. It does not test downloading, speech recognition, or real-source timestamp accuracy.
